subject: Re: NovaCorp private deployment - IP allowlist & egress controls
messages:
From: secops@novacorp.com
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: tom.reynolds@novacorp.com, procurement@novacorp.com
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 14:05:00 -0400
Subject: NovaCorp private deployment - IP allowlist & egress controls

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. As part of our procurement and security review we need a precise allowlist and egress profile for the private (on-prem) connector and the control plane endpoints that Redwood will require. Our security team needs to sign off before we complete the purchase order.

Can you provide the following as soon as possible?
- A CSV we can drop into our firewall team with all required source IPs (static public egress IPs) and destination FQDNs/ports.
- Clarification on which connections are inbound vs outbound from our VPC/on-prem site.
- Guidance on whether IPs rotate (ephemeral) and any rotation cadence or expected maintenance windows.
- Any requirements for SNI inspection, TLS cert pinning, or special client-side proxy configs.
- A short evidence bundle for our audit team: network diagrams, signed statement of custody for IPs, and a sample NAT configuration.

We have a compliance checkpoint on Monday and would appreciate anything you can share before end-of-day Friday.

Regards,
Alex Martinez
Alex Martinez (on behalf of NovaCorp SecOps)
Security Operations
NovaCorp

Attachment: (requested) example_allowlist_template.csv
From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: secops@novacorp.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 15:10:00 -0400
Subject: Re: NovaCorp private deployment - IP allowlist & egress controls

Alex —

Appreciate the clear list. We'll get you a tailored package today with concrete IPs/FQDNs and the evidence bundle. Quick notes up front:
- Redwood Private uses a small control plane surface and a separate data-plane egress footprint. For on-prem deployments you only need to allow outbound/TCP connections to our control plane FQDNs; inbound connections to your environment are not required.
- We can provide a stable set of NAT egress IPs for the control plane and an optional set for inference/data-plane egress when customers use Redwood-managed egress.
- If you run your own NAT/proxy (recommended for auditability), we support both TLS over standard ports and SNI inspection. We do not require cert pinning; mTLS can be enabled on request for private installs.

I'm looping in Laura (Network PM) and Irene (Security) to produce: 1) CSV allowlist, 2) FQDN + port list, 3) short evidence zip with diagrams and handoff statement.

Laura / Irene — can you assemble the files and confirm whether we can commit to static egress IPs for NovaCorp (preferred) or document the rotation policy if ephemeral? Also add any suggested firewall rules (ip, port, protocol, notes).

Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: none (will follow)
From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: secops@novacorp.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 23 Jul 2027 09:02:00 -0400
Subject: RE: NovaCorp private deployment - IP allowlist & egress controls

Hi Alex / team —

Thanks for the checklist. Attached are three items we prepared for NovaCorp: novacorp_allowlist_template.csv, redwood_private_endpoints_fqdn_list.txt, and an evidence bundle egress-evidence-20270722.zip. Summary of the technical requirements (high level first, then copy-paste friendly rows):

High-level summary
- Direction: All connections are outbound from NovaCorp's network to Redwood-managed endpoints (no inbound open ports to NovaCorp required for the control plane).
- Control plane: Stable, low-cardinality egress IP set (we can allocate up to 4 dedicated public IPs per customer for control plane). These IPs are not rotated without coordination.
- Data plane / inference calls: Options: 1) Use NovaCorp-managed egress (preferred) — then outgoing calls appear from your NAT IP(s); or 2) Use Redwood-managed egress — we will provide a documented IP set which may be rotated on planned cadence (we'll notify in advance).
- Ports: 443 (HTTPS/TLS) primarily. Additional ports for metrics/tracing are optional and listed in the attachment.
- TLS/SNI: TLS is required. SNI inspection is allowed; we recommend clients allow SNI passthrough for deep-packet inspection if required. mTLS for control plane is available for an enterprise add-on.

Copy-paste CSV rows (source, destination, ports, proto, note):
- source: <NovaCorp NAT IP(s)>; destination: api-redwood-control-1.redwood-inference.com (TCP 443); proto: TCP; note: control plane API (static IP allocation available)
- source: <NovaCorp NAT IP(s)>; destination: metrics-collector.redwood-inference.com (TCP 443); proto: TCP; note: optional metrics ingestion (can be disabled)
- source: <NovaCorp NAT IP(s)>; destination: model-cache.redwood-inference.com (TCP 443); proto: TCP; note: artifact fetch during startup (short-lived)
- source: <NovaCorp NAT IP(s)>; destination: registry.redwood-inference.com (TCP 443); proto: TCP; note: model registry and version checks

Notes on IP rotation and custody
- Control plane IPs: static (customer-dedicated) by default for Dedicated/Private customers. We will include an IP ownership statement in the evidence bundle.
- Redwood-managed data-plane IPs: these may be rotated quarterly for operational hygiene; notifications via customer console + email 14 days prior and a change log entry.
- If NovaCorp prefers zero-rotation commitments for both control and data plane, we can evaluate via an SLA addendum (legal procurement step).

Firewall rule examples (to drop into your team):
- Allow TCP 443 from <NovaCorp NAT IP range> to api-redwood-control-1.redwood-inference.com (104.198.22.45) — comment: control plane; allow stateful return
- Allow TCP 443 from <NovaCorp NAT IP range> to services.redwood-inference.com (34.120.55.12) — comment: model downloads and telemetry (optional)

Attached file list (included in evidence zip):
- network-diagram-novacorp-redwood.svg
- ip-custody-statement.txt (signed)
- sample-nat-config.txt
- novacorp_allowlist_template.csv
- redwood_private_endpoints_fqdn_list.txt

Next steps / asks
- Please confirm your NAT egress IP(s) and whether you want Redwood-managed data-plane egress. If you want static egress IPs for everything we will route this into procurement/SLA work.
- Let us know if you need mTLS enabled for the control plane; that requires a short PKI exchange and can be completed in our next maintenance window.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Network Product Manager, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Attachment: novacorp_allowlist_template.csv; redwood_private_endpoints_fqdn_list.txt; egress-evidence-20270722.zip
From: tom.reynolds@novacorp.com
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: secops@novacorp.com, procurement@novacorp.com
Date: Fri, 23 Jul 2027 11:30:00 -0400
Subject: Re: NovaCorp private deployment - IP allowlist & egress controls

Laura / Jonas —

Received the package, thanks. A few quick clarifying items before we loop in our firewall team:
1) Can you confirm the control-plane static IPs you propose we allow? The CSV has placeholders; we need the concrete IPv4s to submit to our change board.
2) If we elect Redwood-managed data-plane egress, what is your SLA/notification cadence for IP rotation? Quarterlies are acceptable but procurement wants formal notification windows documented.
3) Is there a recommended change window (UTC range) where an IP rotation or short downtime might occur if needed?

We aim to submit to our change board next Wednesday (27 Jul). If you can provide the control-plane IPs and the formal rotation notification policy by EOD Monday it will keep us on schedule.

Thanks,
Tom Reynolds
IT Infrastructure Lead, NovaCorp
